'''Capri Holdings Limited''' (formerly '''Michael Kors Holdings Limited''') is a [[multinational corporation|multinational]] fashion holding company, incorporated in the [[British Virgin Islands]],<ref name="auto">{{Cite web|url=http://www.capriholdings.com/corporate-overview/default.aspx|title=Capri Holdings Limited - Overview|website=www.capriholdings.com}}</ref> with executive offices in [[London]]<ref name="auto"/> and operational offices in [[New York City|New York]]. It was founded in 1981 by American designer [[Michael Kors]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://dealbook.nytimes.com/2012/02/14/shares-of-michael-kors-as-trendy-as-its-wares/?_r=0|title=Shares of Michael Kors as Hot as Its Wares|last1=Lattman|author-first1=Peter|work=[[The New York Times]]|date=February 14, 2012 |access-date=January 4, 2015}}</ref> The company sells clothes, shoes, watches, [[handbag]]s, and other accessories. In 2015, the company had more than 550 stores and over 1,500 in-store boutiques in various countries.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fierceretail.com/story/michael-kors-plans-rapid-expansion-45-more-north-american-stores/2014-05-30|title=Michael Kors plans rapid expansion with 45 more North American stores|work=FierceRetail|access-date=January 4, 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.malloftheemirates.com/shopping/fashion-luxury/michael-kors.aspx|title=Michael Kors Dubai|publisher=malloftheemirates.com|access-date=June 1, 2016|archive-date=February 13, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140213061756/http://www.malloftheemirates.com/shopping/fashion-luxury/michael-kors.aspx|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Capri is the [[parent company]] of the eponymous Michael Kors brand and [[Jimmy Choo (fashion house)|Jimmy Choo]]. It previously owned [[Versace]], which was sold to [[Prada]] in 2025. [[Tapestry, Inc.|Tapestry]], owner of [[Coach New York]] and [[Kate Spade New York|Kate Spade]], offered to buy Capri for $8.5 billion in 2023,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Fonrouge |first=Melissa Repko, Gabrielle |date=August 10, 2023 |title=Coach owner Tapestry to acquire Michael Kors, Jimmy Choo parent Capri Holdings for $8.5 billion |url=https://www.cnbc.com/2023/08/10/coach-owner-tapestry-to-acquire-capri-holdings-in-8point5-billion-deal.html |access-date=August 10, 2023 |website=CNBC |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Venugopal |first=Aishwarya |date=August 10, 2023 |title=Coach owner's Michael Kors deal creates US giant to take on European luxury rivals |language=en |work=Reuters |url=https://www.reuters.com/markets/deals/coach-parent-tapestry-talks-buy-michael-kors-owner-wsj-2023-08-10/ |access-date=August 10, 2023}}</ref> but called off the acquisition after it was blocked by a federal judge the following year.<ref>{{Cite web  |date=October 24, 2023 |title= Tapestry $8.5 Billion Capri Deal Halted by Judge in FTC Win (3) |url= https://news.bloomberglaw.com/antitrust/tapestry-deal-with-capri-blocked-by-judge-in-ftc-win |access-date=October 24, 2024 |website=Bloomberg |language=en}}</ref>

== Background ==
{{main|Michael Kors}}
Founder Michael Kors enrolled at the [[Fashion Institute of Technology]] in New York City in 1977, but dropped out after nine months.<ref>[http://www.infomat.com/whoswho/michaelkors.html Infomat Michael Kors Biography] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100114225022/http://infomat.com/whoswho/michaelkors.html |date=January 14, 2010}}, Infomat.com, September 10, 2009</ref> Taking a job as a sales person at a boutique called Lothar's across from [[Bergdorf Goodman]] on [[57th Street (Manhattan)|57th Street]] in [[Midtown Manhattan]], he later became both the designer and visual display head for the store.

== History==
[[File:Mk bag.jpg|thumb|A Michael Kors handbag]]
Noticing the displays and garments, Bergdorf's fashion director [[Dawn Mello]] asked if he would show his collection to Bergdorf Goodman's buyers.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://money.cnn.com/2010/09/13/news/companies/michael_kors_fashion.fortune/index.htm |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100915053710/http://money.cnn.com/2010/09/13/news/companies/michael_kors_fashion.fortune/index.htm |url-status=dead |archive-date=September 15, 2010 |title=Michael Kors: Retail's next billion-dollar man |work=cnn.com}}</ref> In 1981, Kors launched his Michael Kors women's label at Bergdorf Goodman. In 1990, the company launched KORS Michael Kors as a licensee.

In 1993, the company was forced into a [[Chapter 11, Title 11, United States Code|Chapter 11]] filing, caused by the closure of the licensing partner for KORS Michael Kors. Putting the KORS line on hold, he designed for other labels before relaunching in 1997 with a lower-priced line, and in the same year was named the first women's [[ready-to-wear]] designer for French house [[Celine (brand)|Celine]].<ref>[https://www.styl.sh/articles/59-the-michael-kors-story The Michael Kors Story] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170729213259/https://www.styl.sh/articles/59-the-michael-kors-story |date=July 29, 2017}}, December 11, 2012</ref>

In 2002, Kors launched his menswear line. Kors left Celine in October 2003 to concentrate on his own brand via holding company Michael Kors Holdings Limited (MKH Ltd), relaunched with a majority $100 million investment from Canadian fashion investor [[Lawrence Stroll]] and his [[Hong Kong]]-based partner [[Silas Chou]], who had previously purchased [[Tommy Hilfiger (company)|Tommy Hilfiger]] in 1989.<ref name="businessoffashion.com">{{cite web|url=https://www.businessoffashion.com/community/people/silas-chou|title=Silas Chouis One of the 500 People Shaping the Global Fashion Industry|website=businessoffashion.com|access-date=September 26, 2018}}</ref><ref name="ejinsight.com">{{cite web|url=http://www.ejinsight.com/20161108-how-tycoon-silas-chou-made-a-fortune-from-two-global-brands/|title=How tycoon Silas Chou made a fortune from two global brands|date=November 8, 2016|website=ejinsight.com|access-date=September 26, 2018}}</ref> [[John D. Idol]] was subsequently appointed CEO of the company, with a shareholding interest. The MICHAEL Michael Kors line was launched in 2004, which included women's handbags and shoes as well as women's ready-to-wear apparel.

In 2011, Stroll and Chou led an [[initial public offering]] in MKH Ltd on to the [[New York Stock Exchange]], making them and Michael Kors billionaires.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/briansolomon/2014/02/04/michael-kors-is-fashions-newest-billionaire/ |title=Michael Kors Is Fashion's Newest Billionaire |work=Forbes |date=January 2014}}</ref> In June 2018, Chou sold the last of his investment in Kors.<ref name="ejinsight.com"/>

In July 2017, MKH Ltd bought [[Jimmy Choo Ltd]] for £897 million.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/business-40714083|title=Jimmy Choo bought by Michael Kors in £896m deal|author=BBC News|date=July 25, 2017|work=BBC.co.uk|access-date=July 25, 2017}}</ref> In September 2018, MKH Ltd  announced a deal to take over [[Versace]]. The Italian fashion group was valued at $2.1 billion.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/michael-kors-near-deal-to-buy-versace-for-around-2-35-billion-1537790108|title=Michael Kors Woos Versace in Push for Foothold in High Fashion|last1=Dalton|first1=Matthew|date=September 24, 2018|work=The Wall Street Journal|access-date=September 25, 2018|last2=Kapner|first2=Suzanne|language=en-US|issn=0099-9660}}</ref> Capri Holdings has planned to up Versace's global retail footprint from approximately 200 to 300 stores.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Michael Kors Holdings Ltd Begins 2019 As Capri Holdings|url=https://www.vogue.co.uk/article/michael-kors-holdings-becomes-capri-holdings|last=Newbold|first=Alice|date=January 2, 2019|website=British Vogue|language=en-GB|access-date=May 19, 2020}}</ref> On January 2, 2019 after closing the deal, the company was renamed to '''Capri Holdings'''.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://news.sky.com/story/versace-bought-by-michael-kors-for-21bn-11508222|title=Versace fashion house bought by Michael Kors for $2.1bn to make super group|work=Sky News|access-date=September 25, 2018|language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://investors.michaelkors.com/news-releases/news-releases-details/2018/Michael-Kors-Holdings-Limited-to-Be-Renamed-Capri-Holdings-Limited/default.aspx|title=Michael Kors Holdings Limited to Be Renamed Capri Holdings Limited|website=investors.michaelkors.com|language=en-CA|access-date=September 25, 2018}}</ref>

[[Tapestry, Inc.]] agreed to acquire Capri for $8.5 billion in August 2023. In April 2024, the [[U.S. Federal Trade Commission]] sued to block the acquisition citing reduced competition between their brands, like Coach and Michael Kors, in the affordable luxury handbag market. It was also concerned that the deal would negatively impact hiring of workers and their wages. Responding to the suit, Tapestry and Capri said they would fight it in court with the aim of closing the transaction by the end of 2024.<ref>{{Cite news |last=D'Innocenzio |first=Anne |date=April 23, 2024 |title=Federal Trade Commission sues to block Tapestry's $8.5B acquisition of Capri |url=https://apnews.com/article/federal-trade-commission-capri-tapestry-0451356264f2d1471546dcac88ad3f2f |publisher=Associated Press}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Repko |first=Melissa |date=April 22, 2024 |title=FTC sues to block Coach parent Tapestry's acquisition of Capri Holdings |url=https://www.cnbc.com/2024/04/22/ftc-sues-to-block-tapestry-acquisition-of-capri-holdings.html |access-date=April 23, 2024 |website=CNBC |language=en}}</ref> The merger was blocked on October 24, 2024.<ref name=bloomberg_10.24.24>{{cite news |last1=Van Voris |first1=Bob |last2=Shen |first2=Yiqin |last3=Dometsch |first3=Chris |title=Tapestry’s $8.5 Billion Capri Deal Halted in FTC Win |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2024-10-24/tapestry-deal-with-capri-blocked-by-judge-in-ftc-win |access-date=October 24, 2024 |work=Bloomberg.com |date=October 24, 2024 |language=en}}</ref> Capri and Tapestry committed to appealing the decision,<ref name=bloomberg_10.24.24/> but called off the merger the following month.<ref>{{Cite news |last1=Mishra |first1=Savyata |last2=Rajesh |first2=Ananya Mariam |date=November 14, 2024 |title=Coach parent Tapestry pulls $8.5 bln bid for Capri after FTC roadblock |url=https://www.reuters.com/markets/deals/coach-parent-tapestry-terminates-85-billion-deal-capri-2024-11-14/ |publisher=Reuters}}</ref>

On April 10, 2025, Capri Holdings finalized the sale of [[Versace]] to [[Prada]] for 1.25 billion euros.<ref>{{cite news |title=Prada acquista Versace per 1,25 miliardi |url=https://www.ilgiornale.it/news/aziende/prada-acquista-versace-125-miliardi-2464464.html |access-date=10 April 2025 |agency=ilgiornale.it |publisher=ilgiornale.it |date=10 April 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Prada to Buy Versace for Nearly $1.4 Billion |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2025/04/10/style/prada-versace-deal.html |access-date=April 10, 2025 |agency=nytimes.com |publisher=nytimes.com |date=April 10, 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Prada compra 100% di Versace da Capri Holdings per 1,25 miliardi di euro |url=https://tg24.sky.it/economia/2025/04/10/prada-versace-accordo |access-date=10 April 2025 |agency=tg24.sky.it |publisher=tg24.sky.it |date=April 10, 2025}}</ref>

== Operations ==
[[File:Michael kors purseshop.jpg|thumb|A Michael Kors purse shop]]
By 2014, the annual revenue for the company was $3.2 billion, with a [[net income]] of $670 million.<ref>{{Cite web|title = Form 10-K|url = https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1530721/000119312514215187/d713190d10k.htm#tx713190_2|website = www.sec.gov|access-date=May 2, 2015}}</ref> By April 2017, the company had 827 full-price or outlet stores and 133 licensed stores.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/money/2017/05/31/michael-kors-store-closures/102341052/|title=Michael Kors to close up to 125 stores as luxury retail woes deepen|work=USA Today|access-date=September 18, 2017|language=en}}</ref> Since 2017, the company said that it would no longer use animal [[fur]] in any of its products.<ref>"Michael Kors Holdings Limited Adopts Fur-Free Policy," Michael Kors Holdings [http://investors.michaelkors.com/news-releases/news-releases-details/2017/Michael-Kors-Holdings-Limited-Adopts-Fur-Free-Policy/default.aspx news release], 15 December 2017.</ref> In 2018, Michael Kors announced two new stores, one in [[Waterloo, New York]],<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.democratandchronicle.com/story/money/business/2018/03/30/panther-pit-closes-pittsford-and-michael-kors-open-waterloo/465477002/|title=Michael Kors to open in Waterloo|work=Rochester Democrat and Chronicle|access-date=March 30, 2018|language=en}}</ref> as well as one in the [[Fairview Park Mall]] in Kitchener, Ontario.

Capri Holdings posted a $1.18 billion loss in fiscal 2025 as revenues  decreased 21% from $5.6 billion to $4.4 billion.

== Trademark protection ==
In Canada, there had been multiple counterfeit Michael Kors bags, wallets, and other items in [[Montreal]], Quebec. In an attempt to end the counterfeit production and to enforce trademark rights, the brand commenced actions against a major network of counterfeit suppliers and vendors, and raided multiple locations throughout the Greater Montreal Area in 2015.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.theglobeandmail.com/report-on-business/luxury-brand-michael-kors-strikes-back-at-quebec-counterfeiters/article24078693/ |title=Luxury brand Michael Kors strikes back at Quebec counterfeiters |work=The Globe and Mail |date=April 23, 2015 |access-date=May 2, 2015}}</ref>
